items.title: Nigeria: Tinubu launches reelection bid amid economic woes
items.summary: President Bola Tinubu promised "a better tomorrow" for Nigerians while kicking off his next electoral campaign, while also blaming his rivals for poverty plaguing Africa's most populous nation Nigeria 's President Bola Tinubu on Saturday formally launched his campaign for a second term "We have prosperity, consistency, growth, recovery and opportunity," Tinubu said at a rally in the northwestern state of Kaduna "You grant me the privilege to promise you once again, there is that promise of a better tomorrow," he added Africa's most populous country will hold its next presidential election in January 2027 . The campaign is expected to focus on Nigeria's economy and security challenges To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video After taking power in 2023, Tinubu sparked anger by scrapping decades-long fuel subsidies — a move that has fueled Nigeria's inflation On Saturday, the incumbent president dismissed criticisms about his economic policies "I hear my opponents talking about hunger and poverty. items.title: Bulgaria holds presidential elections amid divisions over Ukraine war
items.summary: Bulgarians are voting in presidential elections amid security concerns over attacks on ships in the Black Sea. The vote for the largely ceremonial post is seen as a test of the popularity of Prime Minister Rumen Radev Bulgarians are going to the polls in a presidential election on Sunday , where they are choosing between candidates who differ on their approach to the war in Ukraine and how close the country should draw to Moscow The vote comes as drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea off the Bulgarian coast have brought home the significance of the conflict in Ukraine for the former Soviet satellite state Polling stations are open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.

items.title: Gunmen kill at least 10 villagers and loot shops in north-east Nigeria
items.summary: File image of Nigerian police officers Unknown gunmen have raided a remote village in the north-eastern Nigerian state of Taraba, killing at least 10 people, looting shops and setting houses ablaze, police say There are fears the actual death toll is much higher, with eyewitnesses speaking of 20 lives lost and a non-governmental organisation suggesting a toll of as many as 50 The gunmen reportedly swooped on the village of Binnari in the Karim Lamido area mounted on motorcycles just after midday Muslim prayers on Friday in a rampage that went on for up to four hours Police say they are searching for other casualties in the bush but the authorities were accused by Amnesty International of failing to protect rural communities Nigeria continues to face attacks by armed groups across several regions, including the northwest, northeast and central regions The country is also battling a jihadist insurgency in its north-east that has lasted nearly two decades, drawing persistent criticism of the government's handling of insecurity Following the latest incident, police said they recovered…

items.title: Serbia election: Student movement seeks to end Aleksandar Vucic's rule
items.summary: After two years of student-led, anti-corruption protests, Serbia is holding an early parliamentary election that could break long-time populist leader Aleksandar Vucic's grip on the Balkan country Voting began in Serbia on Sunday with a mass student protest movement that has gripped the Balkan country for two years seeking to end the rule of long-time leader Aleksandar Vucic and his party Polls suggest a tight race between Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) and the newly formed, youth-backed Students' List The vote comes after almost two years of student-led protests following the deadly collapse of a train station canopy in the city of Novi ‌Sad in 2024 Demonstrations demanding accountability have since snowballed into Serbia's largest movement since the fall of strongman Slobodan Milosevic in 2000 To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video After calling snap elections last month, Vucic, who has dominated Serbian politics for more than a decade, stepped down as president to run for prime minister The Students'…

items.title: Mozambique: Govt plans 5,541 new civil service hires in 2027, with a budget impact of 1.399 billion meticais
items.summary: According to data from the Economic and Social Plan and State Budget (Plano Económico e Social e Orçamento do Estado – PESOE) compiled today by Lusa, the number of new recruits projected for 2027 represents an increase of 39.9% compared with the 3,962 admissions projected for 2026, while the corresponding budget impact rises by 23.3%, from 1.135 billion meticais (€15.9 million) budgeted for this year to 1.399 billion meticais (€19.6 million) in 2027 Education will continue to account for the largest share of recruitment, with 2,978 admissions planned, equivalent to 53.7% of the total, mainly involving general education teachers. In this sector, the estimated budget impact amounts to 903 million meticais (€12.6 million), corresponding to around two-thirds of the total cost of new admissions planned for next year The proposal also provides for the recruitment of 1,364 employees for the Justice Administration bodies, more than double the 745 admissions planned for 2026.

items.title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds
items.summary: Watch: Doctors told the BBC about the targeting of Sudanese hospitals A BBC investigation has found evidence that Sudanese paramilitary fighters systematically destroyed el-Fasher's healthcare system during their long siege and subsequent takeover of the city in Darfur a year ago UN human rights chief Volker Türk called the findings "deeply disturbing", saying multiple attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on civilian infrastructure, including health facilities, were serious violations of international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes The RSF has rejected the BBC's findings The health minister of the group's civilian-affiliated government dismissed the allegations as propaganda Dr Alaa Eldin Nugud said it was a deliberate attempt by the national army and its allies to smear the RSF's reputation Using sources who were on the ground in el-Fasher, the BBC has found details of at least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and healthcare sites from May 2024 to October 2025 - some hit multiple times Under international law it is illegal to attack health facilities or their…
